item.title: PGA Tour is finally bringing match play to its postseason beginning in 2028 in no-brainer decision
item.description: The PGA Tour Championship will feature a 32-player, two-week match play format starting in 2028, replacing the current FedEx Cup finale structure.
item.content:encoded:
Finally, after years of begging from golf fans, the PGA Tour is introducing match play to its postseason beginning in 2028.

In June, the Tour announced that it will roll out an entirely new competitive structure starting in 2028 with two different tracks, the PGA Tour Championship Series and the PGA Tour Challenger Series. It was assumed that the finale for the Championship Series would include some form of match play, and the Tour made it official with an announcement laying out all of the details on Tuesday.

The Top 90 finishers on the PGA Tour Championship Series points list will retain their membership cards for the following year, and those 90 players will also qualify for the Championship Series Finale. The 90-player, 72-hole stroke play event will essentially serve as the first playoff event, which will then lead into a match play event that will take place across two weeks.

RORY MCILROY GETS SNARKY ON THE RETURN OF LIV GOLF PLAYERS TO PGA TOUR: 'HAVE THEY BROUGHT VALUE?'

The Championship Series Finale will award two separate titles - the season-long points winner and winner of the stroke play event - and the Top 32 players on the final season-long points list will advance to match play.

The two-week event will still be called the Tour Championship, but it will be the first of its kind.

The first week will see the 32-player field split into eight groups of four that will compete in group match play across three days. The top two players in each group will then advance to the second week of the Tour Championship.

In a fun wrinkle worth mentioning, if there is a tie at the conclusion of group play, a playoff will take place to determine who will advance, instead of any sort of margin-of-victory tiebreaker or any others determined on paper.

The second week of match play will feature 16 players who will compete in match play across four days, with the last man standing being the player who manages to win four consecutive matches.

The second week of the Tour Championship will be held at a different venue than the first week of the event. The PGA Tour stated that a full lineup of dates and venues for the 2028 Championship Series will be unveiled on February 22, 2027.

Since the FedEx Cup was first introduced in 2007, serving as the PGA Tour's postseason, the Tour has rolled out multiple formats. From a straightforward season-long points race to giving the points leader a cushion on the leaderboard, and now the simple format of awarding the FedEx Cup to the winner of the Tour Championship, the postseason has long needed a boost.

Making the season finale a match play event – which most would agree is not only the most entertaining but also the best format to determine a champion – was the easiest change to make. PGA Tour commissioner Jay Monahan never got around to making it. Soon-to-be PGA Tour CEO Brian Rolapp announcing the change before he officially assumes his new role on January 1, 2027, can certainly be seen as a surprising sign of what's to come for the Tour and its fans.

The PGA Tour axed its WGC-Match Play event held in Austin, Texas, following the 2023 tournament. While the match play event typically fell at an odd time on the calendar, it was beloved by the overwhelming majority of fans as it was something different.

Having a two-week match play event to close out the year on two separate courses should provide nothing but positive returns for all involved.

item.title: 9/11 victim's identity emerges nearly 25 years later after DNA breakthrough cracks mystery
item.description: A first-of-its-kind forensic genealogy technique helped New York City investigators identify a World Trade Center victim nearly 25 years after 9/11.
item.content:encoded:
Nearly 25 years after the Sept. 11 attacks, a family has finally received an answer after New York City investigators used a first-of-its-kind DNA and genealogy technique to identify a woman killed at the World Trade Center.

The adult woman, whose name is being withheld at her family’s request, is the first World Trade Center victim identified through forensic investigative genetic genealogy, New York City officials announced Sunday.

Her identification marks the 1,654th person identified from remains recovered after the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks, which killed 2,753 people in New York City.

9/11 MUSEUM CEO REFLECTS ON LASTING IMPACT OF TERROR ATTACKS AS AMERICA MARKS 250TH BIRTHDAY

The breakthrough came through a collaboration between the Office of Chief Medical Examiner, and the NYPD’s Investigative Genetic Genealogy Squad. The technique pairs specialized DNA analysis with genealogy research to generate leads that are then confirmed through forensic testing.

"As we approach the 25th anniversary of the horrific September 11 attacks, we honor the nearly 3,000 people whose lives were stolen that day," NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani said in a statement. "We remain committed to the families who have spent 25 years waiting for answers."

REMAINS FOUND IN UTAH DESERT 28 YEARS AGO WITH HELP OF A PSYCHIC FINALLY IDENTIFIED THROUGH DNA GENEALOGY

Forensic investigative genetic genealogy has emerged as a powerful tool in cold cases, allowing investigators to trace family connections from DNA evidence and identify people who may otherwise have remained unknown.

Chief Medical Examiner Dr. Jason Graham said the new method could help advance the city’s long-running effort to identify those killed in the attacks.

WOMAN FOUND IN SHALLOW GRAVE ID’D AFTER 44 YEARS AS MILLIONAIRE TIED TO ESTATE MURDER PLOT

"This sacred commitment is propelled by our dedication to apply the most innovative scientific techniques," Graham said. "FIGG represents a promising new addition to our toolkit."

Officials said they are also using renewed family outreach and continued DNA retesting to link recovered remains to victims already identified.

But the work remains unfinished. About 1,099 World Trade Center victims, roughly 40% of those killed, have yet to be identified.

The woman is the first newly identified World Trade Center victim since August 2025, officials said.

item.title: Pilot marries Vegas-bound couple mid-flight as 178 passengers become wedding guests
item.description: Sara Arroyo Montalvo's Southwest Airlines crew fashioned a toilet paper wedding dress as the captain of the plane officiated the midair ceremony at 35,000 feet.
item.content:encoded:
A couple flying to Las Vegas to elope ended up getting married at 35,000 feet after a Southwest Airlines crew turned their flight into a wedding.

Sara Arroyo Montalvo and her partner had planned to elope privately in Las Vegas when flight attendants learned about their idea and decided to organize a midair ceremony, Montalvo shared in a Facebook post.

The Aug. 13 wedding took place in front of 178 passengers, with the plane's captain — who is also an ordained minister — serving as the officiant, according to the post's caption. 

BRIDE SERVES MCDONALD'S CUSTOMER IN WEDDING DRESS WHILE TYING KNOT AT RESTAURANT: 'HANDING OUT EXTRA SAUCES'

The crew also improvised wedding attire and accessories using items from the plane.

The flight attendants fashioned a veil and one-ply wedding dress from toilet paper for Montalvo, while the bride's bouquet was made using Southwest coffee stir sticks, she wrote in the post.

"Fate couldn't have been more aligned," Montalvo wrote, adding that it was the couple's first time flying with Southwest Airlines.

She thanked the crew for turning what was supposed to be a private elopement into an unexpected celebration.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Thank you from the bottom of our hearts for an unforgettable flight!" she wrote.

Fox News Digital reached out to Southwest Airlines for comment.

The unusual ceremony quickly drew reactions online, with many commenters praising the crew on their thoughtfulness and congratulating the newlyweds on their happy occasion.

"This is the best thing ever!!! Would've [loved] to have been on that flight!" one Facebook user wrote.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

Another commenter called it "about the coolest wedding story I have ever heard of."

Some commenters also raised questions about the legal logistics of getting married in the air, including questions about how a marriage license would be filed and how the officiant would sign the paperwork.

"I wonder what state their marriage license is in?" one commenter asked.

Fox News Digital previously reported on another couple who recently chose an unconventional setting for their wedding. They tied the knot inside the McDonald's restaurant where they both work in Akron, Ohio.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Jamie and George Callicoat initially considered a destination-style wedding before a district manager jokingly suggested they hold the ceremony at the McDonald's.

The restaurant was transformed for the celebration, with friends, family and co-workers gathering as the drive-thru remained open.

The wedding included dinner, a cake and a flower girl who carried petals in a Happy Meal box.

Peter Burke and Teresa Mull of Fox News Digital contributed reporting.

item.title: Dem who urged scandal-plagued candidate to quit now mourns his downfall in pivotal Maine race
item.description: Troy Jackson says he wished nothing had happened to Graham Platner but felt compelled to carry the progressive torch against Susan Collins in Maine.
item.content:encoded:
Maine’s newly anointed Democratic Senate nominee wished "nothing would have happened" to his predecessor, Graham Platner, whose campaign was torpedoed by sexual assault allegations last month.

Troy Jackson, a former logger and Maine state Senate president, slid into the role as Democratic nominee after Platner’s insurgent campaign rapidly unraveled as scandal after scandal piled up, culminating in a sexual assault allegation from his ex-girlfriend that he has since denied.

Jackson had previously run in Maine’s gubernatorial contest, finishing third in the primary earlier this summer. Once Platner exited the race in July, he was quickly chosen by Maine Democrats to succeed him to take on longtime incumbent Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, in a race that could define the balance of power in the Senate.

BERNIE-BACKED MAINE DEMOCRATIC SENATE HOPEFUL SQUIRMS OVER PAST GRAHAM PLATNER SUPPORT

But Jackson never really wanted to run for the Senate, the Midcoast Villager reported, but felt it was important to pick up the mantle of progressive politics that Platner had suddenly dropped.

"I wish nothing would have happened with Graham," Jackson said. "I wish, you know, things would have continued like all that. It would have been much better. But when it did, I just didn't want to see all these people that are looking for somebody to fight for them go away once again broken and hopeless."

Jackson, a fellow progressive who had previously worked on the presidential campaigns of Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., had campaigned alongside Platner and was endorsed by him in his bid for the governor’s mansion.

PLATNER DROPS OUT OF CRUCIAL SENATE RACE AFTER BOMBSHELL RAPE ALLEGATION TORPEDOES CAMPAIGN

When the final allegation hit, he, like several other Democrats both in-state and across the country, called on Platner to exit the race.

"The allegations against Graham Platner are serious, credible, and deserving of full accountability — they cannot and must not be ignored," Jackson said in a statement on X at the time.

"There is a powerful movement of working-class people in the state of Maine," he continued. "For the sake of that movement, and the millions of Americans who have put their trust in it, Graham must now step down."

Jackson has had his own scandals, however.

He has most recently come under scrutiny for his temper following a water bottle-throwing incident while he served in the Senate, and after the discovery of a 1988 police record in which Jackson was alleged to have assaulted a man and pushed his longtime partner, Lana Pelletier, who according to records is his second cousin, during a late-night confrontation.

SUSAN COLLINS DROPS BRUTAL REMINDER OF DEM RIVAL ROCKED BY ACCUSATIONS

Collins declined to weigh in on the police record when asked by Fox News Digital earlier this month, arguing that was up to Jackson.

"But I will say that, based on widespread reporting, it appears that he struggles to control his temper," Collins said.

Meanwhile, there’s an effort afoot to get Platner to register as a write-in candidate in Maine. The deadline to do so is Aug. 25.

A website, writeingrahamforme.com, was launched as op-eds by Scott Niemi have made the rounds in local newspapers in Maine pushing for Platner to submit himself as a write-in, given that under Maine law write-in votes for an undeclared candidate don’t count.

Niemi argued in the Bangor Daily News that writing in Platner would prove to establishment Democrats that they don’t get to "overrule the will of Maine voter," and that because of Maine’s ranked-choice voting system, they could rank Jackson second to "keep the seat competitive."

"If Graham does not have enough votes to advance during tabulation, those ballots are not wasted, they transfer over to Jackson in the next round if he is ranked second," Niemi wrote. "I believe it is a mathematically solid plan to defeat Collins come election time."

item.title: Michael King's home and night game dominance makes Padres the smart pick over struggling Pirates
item.description: Paul Skenes carries a surprising 3.95 ERA into San Diego as the Pittsburgh Pirates face Michael King and the Padres in a critical fight for wild card.
item.content:encoded:
It was a bit of a mixed bag yesterday for results. I had four plays in one game, which is something of a rarity for me. However, I went 3-1 in that game, and I lost the other game. For me, it was a slight profit for the day, but that's because I tend to bet less on player props than I do on full game totals or sides. We go back to the grind today with the matchup between the Pirates and the Padres.

The Pittsburgh Pirates are essentially repeating what they did last year in terms of record. The problem is that the team is not progressing. Last year, the team lost 91 games. It does seem like they will be closer to .500 this year, but coming into this game, they are five games under. They are fourth in their division and 18 games back of first place. If they can get hot before the end of the year, maybe they can make a push for the Wild Card, but they are 7.5 games back of that and have four teams in front of them for the final spot. Even though their hitting has improved, the pitching staff has struggled.

No one has been a bigger surprise struggle this season than today's starter, Paul Skenes. For the year, Skenes is 9-11 with a 3.95 ERA and a 1.14 WHIP. The WHIP is obviously pretty good, but that ERA is far higher than at any point in his short career. He does have 171 strikeouts, so he is still mowing down hitters. It is hard to say exactly what the issue is; he has 41 walks allowed in 139.0 innings this season compared to 42 in 187.2 innings last year, so maybe control is the problem. He has been very good in limited experience against the Padres, holding them to three hits in 24 at-bats.

The San Diego Padres are currently the owners of the last spot in the Wild Card race. With just about a month left, they have to put their foot on the gas pedal and secure that spot. They have run their record to ten games above .500, and this is also reminiscent of last season. They made it to the playoffs via a Wild Card spot last year, and it came after some hot play after the All-Star Break. Last year they started the 2nd half eight games above .500; this year they were at exactly even. Now they are 10 games over.

STAY "FEARLESS" ON THE GO! TAKE TOMI LAHREN WITH YOU. DOWNLOAD THE TLIF PODCAST NOW!

Today they send out Michael King to the hill in hopes that he can give them another victory and put more distance to those teams looking up at them. King has an 8-9 record with a 3.38 ERA and a 1.17 WHIP. He has also been strong with his punchouts, sitting at 41st in the Majors with 128 strikeouts. He's been very good in home starts and night games. In the night games specifically, he has a 2.81 ERA over 93 innings this year. King has held Pirates hitters to just a .250 average over 40 at-bats.

The one guy I see today for a potential player prop is Brandon Lowe. He is just 2-for-13 against King with five strikeouts. I'm not sure I'd feel overly confident in him not getting a hit today, but it is at least an option. For the game, though, we should feel confident backing King here. Skenes is not the Skenes we've seen the past two seasons. King has thrown very well at home and at night. I also trust the Padres bullpen more than the Pirates. Give me the Padres here.

item.title: El-Sayed’s ‘ding-a-ling’ defense of child sex changes becomes instant attack magnet: ‘Not the same, Abdul!’
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed's comparison of circumcision to child sex changes on Jesse Watters' show drew backlash from both left and right-leaning critics.
item.content:encoded:
Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed is catching flak from across the political spectrum for comparing circumcision to child sex changes during a Monday night appearance on "Jesse Watters Primetime."

"So you think it’s okay for a parent to slash his kid’s ding-a-ling off?" Watters asked El-Sayed.

"Are you circumcised?" El-Sayed asked Watters.

ABDUL EL-SAYED GRILLED ON PAST STATEMENTS ON SHARIA LAW AND WHITE SUPREMACY, TAXING THE RICH

"Circumcision’s different than castration," Watters responded.

"It’s a problem that you think you get to decide what happens between a parent, a doctor and a patient," El-Sayed went on. "I’m just saying that, yes, circumcision is surgery on a kid’s ding-a-ling."

Even some on the left didn’t buy into El-Sayed’s attempt to compare sex changes with circumcision.

"This talking point isn’t it,"Ryan Grim, a co-founder of the left-wing outlet DropSite News, wrote in response to a clip of the exchange.

SOCIALIST INSURGENTS EYE MIDWEST GAINS AS DEM CIVIL WAR THREATENS MUST-HOLD SENATE SEAT

"I’m actually agreeing with Jesse Waters…" Andrew Laufer, a New York-based civil rights attorney, posted.

"Abdul El-Sayed just compared circumcision to chopping a kid's entire penis off. Circumcision and castration are not the same, Abdul! Play this on repeat through November," Turning Point USA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet wrote.

"He might be worse than Kamala Harris," conservative pundit Benny Johnson posted.

"Holy crap, Abdul El-Sayed said circumcision is similar to sex change operations on minors," OutKick founder Clay Travis wrote.

Others took opportunities to poke fun at El-Sayed for asking a news host about his penis during a nationally televised interview by making puns.

"Interested to see El-Sayed's pole numbers after this," Washington Free Beacon reporter Chuck Ross quipped.

Some, however, took a more serious tone.

"Sex-rejecting surgeries are not comparable to circumcision, and everyone on this planet knows that, including El-Sayed," the senior policy director of the right-of-center organization Do No Harm said. "Candidates who choose to die on this hill will deserve their election losses."

VETERAN PEDIATRICIAN HAILS MEDICAID SHIFT ENDING YOUTH SEX-CHANGE TREATMENTS: 'THIS IS NOT DENIAL OF CARE'

"El-Sayed obviously knows the difference between circumcision and castration," Singaporean journalist and activist Melissa Chen wrote. "He just can’t say it out loud without pissing off the trans activists who make up his base now … Because he is locked into defending every absurd piece of gender ideology, he can’t actually answer Jesse Waters’ simple question of whether he supports gender-affirming care for under 18 year olds."

Circumcision is an elective surgical procedure that is generally performed on infants, though some medical experts and critics have raised concerns about consent, medical necessity and the risks associated with the procedure.

The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

item.title: Jackson rips into Supreme Court colleagues' 'serious legal error' on Trump mail-in voting order
item.description: Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson warns of election chaos in a 23-page dissent as the Supreme Court lets Trump's mail-voting executive order proceed.
item.content:encoded:
Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson sharply rebuked her colleagues' decision allowing the Trump administration to move forward with parts of its mail-voting executive order, warning that the ruling could create election chaos and leave states trapped between filing legal challenges too early or too late.

"This ruling violates well-established precedents concerning this Court’s equitable discretion and needlessly injects chaos and uncertainty into the upcoming midterm elections," the court's junior liberal justice wrote in a 23-page dissent Monday.

Jackson said the decision "lets another shoe drop in the Kafkaesque nightmare that our precedents have been steadily creating for certain plaintiffs who seek to bring election-related challenges."

The court granted the Trump administration’s request to stay a lower-court injunction that had blocked implementation of portions of President Donald Trump’s March executive order in 23 Democratic-led states and the District of Columbia.

TRUMP SCORES SUPREME COURT WIN ON MAIL-IN VOTING RESTRICTIONS BEFORE MIDTERMS

The unsigned majority opinion did not decide whether the executive order itself is lawful. Instead, the court concluded that the administration was likely to prevail on its argument that the states’ challenge was premature because they had not yet suffered a sufficiently concrete injury.

"The Court’s disposition of this application does not mean that any measure taken by the Government to implement the Order will necessarily be lawful," the majority wrote. "On that score, time will tell."

Jackson took aim at that reasoning, arguing that the states were already confronting election-planning costs, threats of prosecution and uncertainty over possible changes to mail-ballot procedures.

JACKSON PUBLICLY AIRS GRIEVANCES WITH CONSERVATIVE COLLEAGUES OVER TRUMP-ERA RULINGS

She accused the majority of embracing what she called a "Catch-Me-If-You-Can approach" that could make it difficult for states to determine when an election-related challenge is ripe for judicial review.

The court has previously warned against courts changing election rules too close to Election Day. Jackson argued Monday’s decision creates the opposite problem by telling states that some challenges can also come too early.

"The Court does a disservice to all concerned by distorting Article III standing and ripeness principles to issue a ruling that contributes to pre-election chaos instead of quashing it," she wrote.

Jackson also accused the majority of a "lack of situational awareness," arguing that the administration was seeking emergency relief while simultaneously maintaining that the consequences of the executive order remained uncertain.

Trump’s March 31 executive order directs the Department of Homeland Security to take steps toward compiling state-specific lists of U.S. citizens and instructs the attorney general to prioritize certain investigations and prosecutions involving allegedly ineligible voters.

The order also directs the U.S. Postal Service to pursue rules governing mail-in and absentee ballots, including ballot-envelope requirements, tracking barcodes and state-specific voter lists.

FEDERAL JUDGE BLOCKS POSTAL SERVICE FROM CARRYING OUT TRUMP MAIL-IN BALLOT ORDER

The Postal Service outlined plans last week for implementing portions of the order, according to The Associated Press, though the approaching election calendar could limit how much can take effect before November. North Carolina is scheduled to begin sending ballots to military and overseas voters Sept. 4, with other states following soon afterward.

Justice Sonia Sotomayor filed a separate dissent joined by Justice Elena Kagan, arguing that the states already faced sufficiently concrete and imminent injuries to bring their challenge.

The litigation will continue in the lower courts. The Supreme Court’s order stays the Massachusetts injunction while the administration’s appeal proceeds in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit and potentially returns to the Supreme Court.

Jackson closed her dissent by calling the case "not a close call," and arguing that allowing the administration to proceed risked confusion and last-minute disruption ahead of the midterms.

"When the Government’s obvious goal is to interfere with the Plaintiff States’ practices and prerogatives in a manner that the Constitution does not authorize," Jackson wrote, "it is both a serious legal error and a grave misuse of our equitable emergency powers to let the Executive proceed even one step further."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Abdul El-Sayed dodges 'racist NFL' claim, continues defending Colin Kaepernick
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed pivoted to Ford Field ticket prices on Jesse Watters Primetime when pressed on his past claims that the NFL is fundamentally racist.
item.content:encoded:
Socialist Michigan Democrat Abdul El-Sayed, 41, appeared on "Jesse Watters Primetime" to answer for his past shots at football and his claim that the NFL is racist.

When Watters pressed him to defend it, El-Sayed tried to dodge the question before he was eventually tackled.

El-Sayed, the progressive Senate candidate backed by the Democratic Socialists of America, previously blasted football for fostering "toxic masculinity," "bro culture," and "racism, misogyny, and homophobia."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

He also branded the NFL fundamentally racist and insisted the grifting ex-QB Colin Kaepernick deserved more years in the league.

It showed just how separated El-Sayed is from the common American.

He told Watters:

"Look, I think for Colin Kaepernick, I think he should have had several more years in the NFL. Now I think he's a pretty damn good quarterback. I think, unfortunately, he lost a lot of time.

EL-SAYED DARES GOP RIVAL TO NO-PADS FOOTBALL SHOWDOWN AS SENATE FEUD TURNS PERSONAL

"But the bigger question right now when it comes to football, look, I know you guys like to think I don't like football, but I'm happy to line up against anybody who thinks that I don't like football.

"And I'll just tell you, the bigger issue that we have for football right now is, I looked at ticket prices to try and go and see a game with my family. It's astronomical through the roof.

"Now, I think football used to be the kind of thing that you could enjoy with people... That's gone for too many people. I want to talk about football. I want talk about access to football."

About those old claims that the NFL is racist ... Watters called out El-Sayed's side-stepping of his old comments.

ABDUL EL-SAYED GRILLED ON PAST STATEMENTS ON SHARIA LAW AND WHITE SUPREMACY, TAXING THE RICH

"I asked you if you thought the NFL was racist because you said the NFL is racist and now you're talking about ticket prices. The NFL is too expensive you don't agree. All right, so you don't think it's racist anymore. I get it I'm glad you don't think the NFL's racist anymore."

El-Sayed ran back the same play, which was to dodge.

"I'm just saying, most people can't afford that. Bigger issue with the NFL, you won't talk about the NFL. The bigger issue with NFL is too many people can afford it. You probably can, and I know that you're in New York, so you have like two teams that play in the same place. So you get two options. But I'm saying that here in Michigan, we've got one team and most people can't watch them in the stadium. And I'd like to make it more affordable."

"All right, so you dodged, you dodgy again," Watters responded.

El-Sayed once had plenty to say when calling football toxic and racist.

Asked to defend those claims on live TV, the candidate chose to talk ticket prices instead.

item.title: Federal judge slaps down Ghislaine Maxwell petition for new trial as ‘rambling,’ ‘meritless’
item.description: Judge Paul Engelmayer called Ghislaine Maxwell's post-conviction challenge "meritless" and "frivolous," finding trial evidence against her "overwhelming."
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge rejected Ghislaine Maxwell’s latest effort to overturn her conviction, blasting her petition as "lengthy and rambling" and finding her claims "all meritless" and "all or almost all" frivolous.

U.S. District Judge Paul A. Engelmayer denied Maxwell’s post-conviction challenge in an opinion filed Monday in the Southern District of New York and made public Tuesday, writing that the evidence against the convicted Jeffrey Epstein associate at trial was "overwhelming."

Maxwell, representing herself, had moved to vacate her conviction and 20-year prison sentence, alleging that her constitutional rights were violated at trial and sentencing.

TODD BLANCHE SAYS 'NO CLOSED INVESTIGATIONS' IN EPSTEIN CASE, VOWS DOJ WILL PURSUE NEW SUSPECTS

Engelmayer said the vast majority of her arguments were procedurally barred because she either raised and lost them on direct appeal or could have raised them earlier but did not.

The judge also shot down Maxwell’s reliance on material released under the Epstein Files Transparency Act, finding that the purported new evidence did not support her claims. The supposedly "new" evidence was largely irrelevant to  Maxwell 's case, the judge said.

FORMER ATTORNEY GENERAL PAM BONDI HAILS TRUMP ADMINISTRATION'S 'JUSTICE AND TRANSPARENCY' ON EPSTEIN FILES

"To the extent it is relevant, far from exculpating her, it incriminates her or reinforces the correctness of the legal rulings Maxwell challenges," Engelmayer wrote.

"The Court accordingly denies Maxwell’s petition," he concluded.

Maxwell was convicted in December 2021 on five felony counts stemming from her participation with Epstein in the sexual abuse of young girls over the course of a decade.

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Denmark's left-wing PM warns: 'Big enemy has started to grow from within' as Europe faces migrant reckoning
item.description: Mette Frederiksen's stance on Denmark immigration and border control puts her at odds with Spain's PM, as she names failed integration and Islamist extremism as key threats.
item.content:encoded:
Denmark's left-wing prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, has sent shock waves throughout the European left after recent comments about the Scandinavian nation's — and the continent's — failure to deal with radical Islam among migrant communities.

Her comments come after the mass migration chaos in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta, when Frederiksen criticized the actions of Spain's leftist leader, Pedro Sánchez, during a special session on Ceuta in the Danish Parliament. 

Responding to a question from a far-left legislator on Denmark’s apparent lack of "solidarity" with Spain against "anti-democratic forces" pressuring Europe, Frederiksen said, "If we talk about undemocratic forces, then Russia is our biggest enemy. The problem is that a big enemy has started to grow from within, and it is foreigners who have come to Europe," according to an English translation.

MIGRANT CRISIS PUSHES ITALY TO RESTORE BORDER CHECKS WITH SPAIN, TESTING EUROPE'S OPEN-BORDER SYSTEM

While not singling out Denmark's integrated immigrant population, she continued, "It is Hamas supporters. It is people who commit terror against European societies. It is people who do not recognize our fundamental European values. It is people who sympathize with some of the darkest forces in this world. So, Europe is threatened. The problem is that we are threatened both from outside and now from within, but it is not because of a disagreement between the Danish and Spanish governments, but because of people with an Islamic background who do not want the open, free European society, unfortunately."

Sweden-based foreign policy expert and author Daniel Schatz told Fox News Digital, "What is striking is not that a conservative politician is talking about illegal immigration, failed integration and Islamist extremism, it is that one of Europe’s leading center-left prime ministers is saying it in such blunt terms. That tells you how far the European immigration debate has shifted."

PORTUGAL ENACTS 'BURQA LAW' LARGELY PROHIBITING FACE COVERINGS IN PUBLIC

Frederiksen came to power in Denmark’s 2019 elections on what Reuters called a "platform of radical reforms to reach climate targets, lowering the pension age for manual workers - and stricter migration policies." Denmark already had some of the strongest asylum laws in Europe before 2019, including a 2018 law targeting "parallel societies." That law allowed the government to "demolish or sell off social housing areas where more than half of residents are from a ‘non-Western’ background," if certain criteria were met, and refugees in those areas are not eligible for family reunion.

In 2021, Frederiksen introduced a new deportation law allowing for refugees to be returned to their country of origin, if Denmark deemed it safe, even if Denmark had no diplomatic relations with that country, and even as the European Commission deemed Danish legislation on transferring asylum seekers to third countries while their claims were processed "incompatible with EU law."

Since June, Frederiksen has been a leading voice in opposition to the immigration policies of Spain’s Pedro Sánchez, telling Parliament, "It is no secret that I and the Spanish Prime Minister deeply disagree on immigration policy… I and we will not accept that Danish society has to pay the price for decisions in Spain that we fundamentally disagree with."

On Aug. 1, Frederiksen joined conservative Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and 20 other EU government leaders in a letter saying the EU "cannot allow mass crossings, the instrumentalization of migration or other hybrid threats to create the perception that illegal entry into the European Union is possible."

ITALY-SPAIN BORDER FEUD EXPOSES EUROPE’S DEEPENING IMMIGRATION DIVIDE

The two, currently the only female heads of government in the EU, followed that letter with an Aug. 10 joint statement saying they "are both proud of Europe’s Christian cultural heritage and we want to protect it. We expect that those who arrive in our countries and choose to make Europe their home respect our values and do not try to impose ways of life that we do not share. We believe that this is the right path to protect Europe and our common values. And we believe that millions of Europeans share this conviction."

Emma Schubart of the Henry Jackson Society told Fox News Digital, "Frederiksen is right to name the ‘enemy within’. Europe has spent years pretending that uncontrolled migration and failed integration come without consequences. They do not… Parallel societies have taken root, Islamist extremism has been allowed to fester and support for groups such as Hamas is no longer confined to the margins. Denmark understands the cost."

Daniel Schatz said Frederiksen "is essentially arguing that Europe faces threats from two directions: Russia from outside and anti-democratic extremism from within. For a center-left European leader, that is remarkably strong language." He noted Frederiksen’s "political formula has been straightforward: protect Denmark’s generous system of public benefits and social services, control the border and deny the populist right a monopoly on immigration. For an American audience, that is probably the most important thing to understand about the Danish model."

Frederiksen’s position is important, he said, because she did not move politically "because Danish voters suddenly became concerned about immigration. She moved because she realized years ago that many of them already were." He added, "The important distinction is that this is not an argument that immigrants are inherently criminal. It is an argument that a democratic society must be willing to confront failed integration when it occurs."

Schubart added, "Other leaders now need to show the same courage, secure their borders, deport those with no right to remain and make clear that integration into our laws and values is not optional."

Reuters contributed to this report.

item.title: Ohio man charged over graphic threats to kill Trump, behead GOP lawmaker
item.description: The FBI arrested an Ohio man who allegedly sent graphic death threats to Jewish Republican Rep. Randy Fine and President Donald Trump via email.
item.content:encoded:
An Ohio man was arrested by the FBI after allegedly making graphic threats against a Jewish Republican congressman and calling for the death of President Donald Trump.

Alex Justin Miller, 26, is accused of sending a "true threat" to Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., and his family, according to the Department of Justice (DOJ). 

A copy of the message separately obtained by Fox News Digital shows Miller allegedly called Fine and his family "Nazi f—-s" and said he would burn their house down, pledging he would "never stop until your head is hanging from the rooftops of the White House." His message ended with "DEATH TO RANDY FINE AND DEATH TO DONALD TRUMP."

Miller was charged with interstate transmission of a threat to injure by the U.S. Attorney in the Middle District of Florida and faces up to five years in prison if convicted, the DOJ said.

FAA EMPLOYEE CHARGED WITH ALLEGEDLY THREATENING TO KILL PRESIDENT TRUMP IN EMAIL TO WHITE HOUSE

The incident was investigated by the FBI and the Brevard County Sheriff's Office with assistance from the Secret Service and Capitol Police, the DOJ said.

"It was so graphic. It says, 'I'm gonna murder you. I'm going to cut your head off. I won't stop,'" Fine told Fox News Digital. "I reported it immediately. I unfortunately have learned what the difference is between a nasty message and a death threat, and this clearly was a death threat."

The full message read: "Dear fat--- piece of s---stain, I cannot wait to take a trip to you lovely home and light the whole place on fire and murder you and your entire family in the middle of the night while you sleep. I hope you disgusting Nazi f---s sleep with one eye open for the rest of your life because I will NEVER stop until your head is hanging from the rooftops of the White House. You deserve 10000% to be beheaded and have your body paraded through the streets. DEATH TO RANDY FINE AND DEATH TO DONALD TRUMP!!" 

Fine said he received the threat via email on the morning of primary Election Day in the Sunshine State. He also said it reinforced his belief that federal officials need more protection.

"I don't know what this person's motives were for writing this, but it's someone not from Florida. So, you know, this was not a local constituent that was upset," he said. "I do think members of Congress need more security than we oftentimes get."

FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY THREATENING TO KILL TRUMP, RUBIO AND BONDI

He added that law enforcement found and arrested the man within 36 hours.

"I'm incredibly grateful to the U.S. attorney, the FBI, the Capitol Police, and all the law enforcement in Florida who took this seriously. The bottom line is, don't do this. Don't write messages like this to elected officials, Republican or Democrat. You want to call us bad people? Be my guest, but do not do this sort of thing," Fine said.

item.title: I feared AI would leave my community behind. Now I see a path to prosperity
item.description: The AI boom demands 130,000 additional skilled trades workers by 2030, creating massive opportunities for electricians, plumbers and HVAC technicians.
item.content:encoded:
There has been worry of late that AI may eliminate jobs. I have seen the power of AI, and I can understand why some sectors are worried.  I have even worried that this ongoing AI revolution may leave behind the troubled youth in my South Side of Chicago neighborhood. For the past several years, I have been building this massive Leadership and Economic Opportunity Center to teach young people the trades as a way out of poverty and violence. And I’m sitting here, wondering if I made a mistake. Have I created something that is outdated? I admit I felt this panic deep within my soul. Was I handing my youth a caveman tool when they needed the latest technology?

I wondered how we would adapt to this ever-changing world that changes so fast that sometimes I can’t even remember who was in the news last week. So I took a walk through the walls of the new building. It’s beautiful. It brings me such joy to see the rooms and the promises of opportunity that come with them. We have rooms for the trades in every aspect of construction, from wood cutting to plumbing. We have rooms for creating new electricians. We’ve also got rooms for creating HVAC workers and fiber technicians, and more. We’ve got amazing equipment for our youth to train on. But was all of this for nothing? Did time pass us by?

I did not create this building to leave another empty shell on the South Side of Chicago. Just down the street from us, Walgreens and McDonald’s fled, and there are boarded-up buildings. There are no grocery stores, and we’re a true food desert where fried foods are often our only quick and easy option. The rates of homeownership here are abysmal. Despite low home prices, some blocks have homeownership rates as low as 14% to 24%. We have a poverty rate of 40% to 51%, depending on which block you go to. And don’t even get me started on our local schools.

DIVINE PURPOSE HELPED BRING CHICAGO’S MOST-DANGEROUS BLOCK BACK TO LIFE

That is why I am so desperate to bring a symbol of hope to my community through the building of this community center. I still felt that quiet desperation as I walked past the construction workers at work. I came upon a young man who had finished his job here. After thanking him for his contribution, I asked him where he was going next. He explained that he had secured work for a major AI manufacturing facility in a nearby township. As he told me more and more, I thought to myself: There’s a building boom.

When we think of AI, we think of the Silicon Valley story about white-collar workers. The media is full of headlines about white-collar workers afraid of losing their jobs. But at the same time, I was also noticing, in my layman’s view of the world, that AI could potentially be the wealth-of-knowledge generator that places practical expertise directly in the hands of young people failed by the current systems. In other words, AI could help my youth leapfrog gaps in local schooling and training by enabling self-sufficiency faster.

THE AI REVOLUTION THREATENS OFFICE JOBS, BUT REVIVES DEMAND FOR SKILLED TRADES

I also began, thanks to my conversation with the young construction worker, to see that many people were missing the big opportunity here. While AI may transform or eliminate certain desk jobs, it is also a world unto itself that must be built. We’re talking about data centers, power grids, fiber networks and advanced manufacturing facilities. 

Who is going to help build this revolution? I looked down from the roof of my community center at the young people on the sidewalks and prayed that it would be them and their peers.

This AI boom will require, for many years, electricians, HVAC technicians, construction workers, plumbers, pipefitters, fiber technicians and other skilled tradespeople. I recently drove out to see some of these facilities being built, and they’re massive. The world is changing before our eyes, and we’re entering an entirely new era of infrastructure.

A SOUTHERN STATE JUST TOOK THE TOP SPOT IN ONE OF THE WORLD’S FASTEST-GROWING INDUSTRIES

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has called this the largest infrastructure buildout in human history. Major tech companies are projected to spend roughly $700 billion this year alone on AI-related facilities. This will only increase as more and more of us adopt AI. And it is happening as hundreds of data centers are under construction or planned across the United States. One analysis estimates the nation will need 130,000 to 140,000 additional skilled trades workers by 2030 just to support AI infrastructure—before accounting for housing, hospitals and energy projects competing for the same talent.

This demand has created an urgency to develop new workers. The Bureau of Labor Statistics projects electrician employment to grow 9% from 2024 to 2034, a rate much higher than average. The bureau projects about 81,000 openings each year. HVAC mechanics and installers are projected to grow 8%, which translates to roughly 40,100 openings annually. Plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters are expected to see about 44,000 openings per year. 

WANT TO STRENGTHEN AMERICA'S ECONOMY? THE KEY INVESTMENT IS HIDING IN PLAIN SIGHT

In May 2026, the construction industry reported approximately 298,000 job openings. Specialty-trade contractors already employ more than 565,000 electricians and 349,000 plumbers, pipefitters and steamfitters. The Associated Builders and Contractors estimates the industry needs roughly 349,000 net new workers in 2026 alone. In data-center hotspots, skilled-trades wages already carry a 7% premium overall, with plumbers and pipefitters seeing gains as high as 20%.

More importantly, the median annual pay for these jobs is solid, at around $62,000 to $72,000. This may not seem like a lot, but for a kid who has known nothing but generational poverty, this is the way out of the culture of dependency. 

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Yes, one job like this can end that vicious, soul-sucking cycle that has kept so many of us stuck in the permanent Black underclass. These careers build assets, they restore dignity and pride, and they give people a stake in America.

At first, I feared that the AI revolution would leave my youth behind. But now I’m more convinced than ever that this is the greatest opportunity to come along.

I was part of the Great Migration myself, the very tail end of it. My mother and her husband moved from a tiny town in Tennessee to Muncie, Indiana, for better jobs in industrial factories. When I visited them and later moved to Indiana, I was exposed to a world of more opportunities. 

I see this cycle of life coming back around today, and I’m determined more than ever to push my youth onto this AI opportunity wagon. As they say, this is their chance to strike it rich in America.

item.title: ‘Send help’: LA GOP leader issues desperate appeal after Dem mayor’s campaign vid shocks viewers
item.description: LA County GOP Chair Roxanne Hoge says Karen Bass's viral 6-to-1 matching funds video reveals how Democrats codified electoral 'shenanigans' into law.
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE: Los Angeles County GOP Chair Roxanne Hoge issued an impassioned appeal for Republicans to "send help" to Democratic-controlled California, describing what she sees as rampant corruption in the state and saying most people "can't understand the level of obsession they have with controlling our lives."

In an interview with Fox News Digital, Hoge addressed the online reaction to a recent viral video posted by Democratic Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass in which the mayor said the city government would match six times every dollar donated to her re-election campaign. While some social media users expressed shock, Hoge said she was not surprised.

"The rest of the country doesn't understand what we're living under here," she told Fox News Digital.

"The number one thing people need to understand about Los Angeles in particular and California in general is that they've codified all of their shenanigans," she explained. "What normal people consider cheating or weirdness in the electoral process? It's all in the rules [here]."

LOS ANGELES PROPOSAL TO ALLOW NONCITIZENS TO VOTE IN LOCAL ELECTIONS SPARKS ONLINE BACKLASH

In a recent viral social media post, Bass, Los Angeles’ 72-year-old progressive mayor, said that "when you donate to our campaign, the city can match your donation 6 to 1," adding, "If you donate $5, the city turns it into $35."

Bass said that "thanks to LA’s super match program, every qualified donation from Los Angeles residents is matched six to one by the city." She added that after this year’s mayoral primary, in which Republican candidate Spencer Pratt garnered significant support, "we had to start over from scratch."

"So, we need you to rush in your matching donation right now, to help fuel this campaign," she said.

Social media users questioned and criticized Bass’ comments.

Conservative activist Billboard Chris commented, "How is it legal to take money from Los Angeles taxpayers to fund your own re-election campaign?" Commentator Matt Van Swol wrote, "Can someone please explain to me like I’m 5 years old how this is not COMPLETELY illegal?????"

KAREN BASS RIPPED AFTER SUGGESTING TAXPAYER-FUNDED DENTAL CARE FOR METH USERS

Author Michael Shellenberger simply wrote, "This is grotesque."

"Is this a JOKE?!?" wrote well-known Los Angeles doctor and political commentator Houman David Hemmati. "Why on EARTH are LA City taxpayers, who can’t even afford to clean up their streets or have water in their fire hydrants, forced to match contributions to Bass’ Mayoral reelection campaign 6:1?!? … HUH?! Insanity!"

Hoge, however, said the matching-funds program Bass describes in her campaign video is legal under city law. Los Angeles voters approved a public campaign-financing system in 1990 that the City Council later expanded into today’s six-to-one matching-funds program. Donations are subject to caps and eligibility rules.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"Voters passed something that sounded so good; they always sound so good at the beginning. Public financing matching funds for campaigns on a one-to-one basis. That seems great, right?" she said. "And then it transmogrifies … into what we have today, this many-headed hydra of insanity where taxpayers are on the hook for $6 for every dollar raised by a city of L.A. candidate."

She noted that the rule applies not only to mayoral campaigns but also to City Council campaigns, adding that they "Have many active [Democratic Socialists of America] members currently sitting and running."

Hoge said "the message that Karen Bass is sending is the same message that those of us who live here behind the blue curtain have been getting for decades."

"And that is, ‘Forget it, Jake, it's Chinatown. Don't try to go against City Hall,’" she said.

SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES'

"We saw Spencer Pratt mount a very strong argument for sanity and good governance. It wasn't partisan, what he was saying. It was pure common sense, and they rose up because they were threatened."

Fox News Digital reached out to Bass’ campaign and office for comment.

Despite California’s political landscape, Hoge urged Republicans not to write off America’s most populous state as a lost cause.

"California is totally worth fighting for because it is an absolute gem," she said, adding, "We are living with people who gleefully would reach into the shower and change the temperature while you're having a bath."

Addressing Republicans directly, she said, "We belong to the leave me alone party."

"California, being in the west, is the ultimate place where you should be free to write your own story. And that, I think, is the number one thing people have to remember," she said. "They need to send help."

item.title: Outgoing House Democrat Al Green files another impeachment resolution targeting President Donald Trump
item.description: Democratic Rep. Al Green of Texas, who lost a Democratic primary runoff earlier this year, filed a new resolution targeting President Donald Trump for impeachment.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Al Green, D-Texas, who has repeatedly targeted President Donald Trump for impeachment, renewed his effort by filing a new impeachment resolution on Monday.

"Our country and the lives of people within it are at risk as President Donald John Trump is a great threat to the United States democratic republic, its Constitution, and democracy, violating Article II, Section 1, Clause 8 of the United States Constitution and its mandate to faithfully execute the office of President of the United States and, to the best of his ability, preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution of the United States," the document declares.

The resolution accuses Trump of "abusing the powers of the presidency by operating United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) as his vicious, quota-driven, unaccountable paramilitary police forces, transgressing with anonymity and secrecy, assaulting people, committing and covering up unjustified killings of civilians (including Renée Good, Alex Pretti, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero) with impunity (acting as judge, jury, prosecutor, and executioner), terrorizing communities, and brazenly and wantonly devolving the United States democratic republic into an authoritarian regime, where unjustified killings and coverups by ICE and CBP are normalized."

AL GREEN RESPONDS TO JULY 4 QUESTION WITH RENEWED CALL TO IMPEACH TRUMP

In a statement provided to Fox News Digital on Tuesday, White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said, "This type of garbage is contributing to our law enforcement officers facing a more than 1,300% increase in assaults against them. The brave men and women of ICE and CBP put their lives on the line to arrest murderers, rapists, pedophiles, gang members, and terrorists. Al Green should be thanking President Trump and our law enforcement for delivering the largest decrease in violent crime in American history."

A Department of Homeland Security spokesperson slammed Green in a statement provided to Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

"These tired allegations are unequivocally FALSE. The only things more inconsequential than Rep. Green's impeachment resolutions are his eleven terms in Congress," the spokesperson asserted. "This type of rhetoric is contributing to our officers facing coordinated campaigns of violence against them including a more than 1,300% increase in assaults against them, 3,300% increase in vehicle attacks, and an 8,000% increase in death threats. President Trump and Secretary Mullin will always stand with our ICE law enforcement officers.

"DHS law enforcement officers are trained to use the minimum amount of force necessary to resolve dangerous situations to prioritize the safety of the public and our officers. Officers are highly trained in de-escalation tactics and regularly receive ongoing use of force training. The latest ICE use of force policy is available here.

"Under President Trump and Secretary Mullin, ICE is targeting the worst of the worst. Nearly 70% of ICE arrests are of illegal aliens charged or convicted of a crime in the U.S. There is no quotas for arrests. The men and women of ICE law enforcement are patriots who put their lives on the line every single day to arrest the worst of the worst including murderers, rapists, pedophiles, gang members, and terrorists," the statement concluded.

Fox News Digital also reached out to ICE and CBP on Tuesday.

Given that Republicans currently hold the majority in both chambers of Congress, his latest impeachment push likely won't succeed.

REP. AL GREEN TELLS HOMELAND SECURITY SEC. MULLIN TO 'SHUT UP' AFTER CALLING HIM A RACIST AT HEARING

But in a letter to the president, Green said, "Mr. President, I am well aware of the fact that you will be defended by persons who will say, ‘The House won’t impeach, and if it did, the Senate won’t convict.’ Sir, my response is that articles of impeachment that are not approved by Congress can express on-the-record disapproval of presidential actions and demonstrate that there are some of us watching and willing to act."

Green has fielded impeachment resolutions multiple times across both of Trump's White House terms.

The congressman, who has served in the House since 2005, lost a Democratic primary runoff to Rep. Christian Menefee in May.

TRUMP COULD FACE IMPEACHMENT IF DEMOCRATS SEIZE HOUSE MAJORITY, GOP LEADER WARNS

The House impeached Trump twice during his first term, but in both cases, the Senate vote did not meet the threshold necessary for conviction. The Senate's vote on the second impeachment took place after Trump had already departed from office.

item.title: Florida-led operation rescues 163 children around globe in historic state sweep, hunts suspected predators
item.description: Attorney General James Uthmeier announced Operation Statewide Shield recovered 163 children across five continents in five days this August.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: A multi-agency effort in Florida has recovered 163 children — from 2 months old to 17 — across five continents during Operation Statewide Shield, Attorney General James Uthmeier announced Tuesday.

item.title: 3 things Democrats don’t want you to know about AI and data centers
item.description: AI data centers are reviving small towns like Ellendale, N.D., bringing jobs, tax revenue and lower electricity bills to communities left behind.
item.content:encoded:
Everywhere you look, people are talking about artificial intelligence (AI). It’s on your TV. It’s on your radio. It’s on your social media feed. And it seems like Democrats and their media allies are doing their very best to scare you away from it by telling you that AI is going to destroy the environment, take your job and hike up your utility bills. But anytime Democrats and liberal journalists are in lockstep on an issue, that should set off your alarm bells – why do they want you to be scared?

The reason is that left-wingers want to seize control of AI for their own political purposes. But don’t take my word for it. As Democratic strategist Jesse Ferguson put it: "the fight for Democrats is not ‘we are for AI’ or ‘we are against AI.’ That framing is a trap. The fight is over control."

Democrats and their media allies want to scare people about AI in order to justify putting woke bureaucrats in charge, where they can force AI to advance their political agenda. Remember how Big Tech companies became Democrats’ political censors under Joe Biden? That’s what Democrats want to do with AI – turn it into a political weapon.

AI HAS AN OPINION AND IT USUALLY LEANS LEFT. YOU HAVE A RIGHT TO KNOW ITS AGENDA

THE NEXT AMERICAN BOOM COULD BE HERE — UNLESS WASHINGTON REGULATES IT TO DEATH

AI and data centers are revitalizing the pro-Trump small towns that make up the heartbeat of America – the exact small towns that were left for dead when offshoring hollowed out the American manufacturing industry.

Take Ellendale, N.D., for example. Decades of economic decline left the town with barely 1,000 residents as of the most recent census. As the school superintendent put it: "We were a dying little town." But then a data center arrived – and everything changed.

META OFFERS PAID TRAINING FOR AI DATA CENTER JOBS

Jobs went through the roof. Tax revenue did, too, as one columnist recounted: "Ellendale can now afford to repave its streets, renovate its senior center, finance a new public-safety complex, establish walking trails and refurbish its historic opera house."

That’s not a one-off story. In Louisiana’s Richland Parish – a community that voted for President Donald Trump by a nearly 40% margin in 2024 – a Meta data center brought in so much tax revenue that local teachers received bonuses of $50,000.

A SOUTHERN STATE JUST TOOK THE TOP SPOT IN ONE OF THE WORLD’S FASTEST-GROWING INDUSTRIES

Or consider rural Virginia’s Louisa County, where data center development didn’t just bring jobs – it brought tax cuts, too, thanks to the surge in tax revenue from the data centers. And then there’s the little red town of Quincy, Wash., where an investment surge from data centers has brought a new $120 million high school, a 79% decrease in the poverty rate, new sidewalks, more police officers on the beat, property tax cuts and more.

In short: the total revival of the town. So, it’s no surprise that Wells Fargo analyst Ohsung Kwon’s research concluded that communities with data centers are seeing "significant economic benefits" – both during data center construction and for years afterwards.

Nobody is telling you the truth about water, utility bills and what data centers have to do with them. Not the electric companies, not the liberal media and certainly not elected Democrats like New York Democrat Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez.

THE REAL REASON YOUR ELECTRIC BILL IS SOARING THIS SUMMER WILL SURPRISE YOU

The power companies were quick to scapegoat data centers for cost increases that began well before the very first version of ChatGPT was released on Nov. 30, 2022. But in case there was any doubt, President Donald Trump’s Ratepayer Protection Plan guarantees that AI companies pay their own way, ensuring that Americans are protected from rate increases due to data center developments. More than 80% – and counting – of Americans are covered under the Ratepayer Protection Plan.

In some cases, data center developments can actually lead to lower bills for neighboring residents. A June 2026 study found that data center developments indeed led to modest decreases in electricity rates. That might seem counterintuitive at first, but the reality is that electric companies have huge fixed costs – costs that they have to pay whether they have one customer or one million – in which case having a massive customer (data centers) absorb the lion’s share of those fixed costs means fewer costs to spread among everyone else.

THE BIGGEST THREAT IN AMERICA'S RACE WITH CHINA ISN'T BEIJING, TECH EXECUTIVE WARNS

Reality bears this out as well. In Ellendale, N.D., electricity bills were $250 lower per customer thanks to their new data center. Who wouldn’t want an annual $250 discount on their electric bill?

The narrative about water use might be the most misleading one of all. It’s largely due to a bestselling book – "Empire of AI" – that was so factually flawed that it suffered multiple corrections. Even the Washington Post observed that Empire of AI’s calculations were off by a "thousandfold."

DEMOCRATS SOUND ALARM OVER AI JOB APOCALYPSE — BUT LABOR MARKET ISN'T FOLLOWING SCRIPT

And not only was the book wrong, but it quickly became outdated, too, because data centers are moving to closed-loop cooling systems in which "day-to-day cooling doesn’t depend on adding water" and "community water usage for cooling the data center is effectively zero." Or, as Nvidia’s chief sustainability officer put it: "The water consumption challenge for data centers is largely solved."

For decades, America’s biggest companies have enjoyed an enormous built-in advantage: They can afford armies of programmers, analysts, marketers, lawyers and consultants that small businesses simply can’t. AI is leveling the playing field for small businesses by giving them access to the same arsenal of weapons at a fraction of the cost.

So, it’s no wonder that Russell Kaplan, the president of Cognition AI, said he’s anticipating "an explosion in small businesses" thanks to the AI revolution. But don’t take his word for it: small business owners themselves tell a similar story. The Small Business Cash Flow Trend Report found that 61% of small-business owners report using AI, with 91% of those users reporting a positive impact on their business.

It’s not just small-business owners, either. Blue-collar workers are seeing a jobs boom thanks to AI – and these jobs are paying better, too. "Dirty Jobs" host Mike Rowe recounted in a podcast interview how, when he visited a data center in Plano, Texas, he was stunned by the wealth that was flowing to blue-collar workers. "The electricians that I interviewed and met two months ago in a data center in Plano, Texas, all under 30 years old, all making $240,000 to $280,000 a year, all with as much overtime as they want," Rowe said. Everybody wins when the American worker succeeds – everybody except socialists who depend on keeping people poor.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

The world is changing pretty quickly. There’s no doubt about that. But the next time somebody tries to scare you into opposing American AI dominance, ask yourself three questions: 1) Who is trying to make you feel that way? 2) Why do they want you to feel that way? And 3) Are they telling you the truth?

The answers to those questions will reveal a lot.

item.title: California sheriff doubles down on seizing ballots as state Supreme Court hears whether he must return them
item.description: Sheriff Chad Bianco still holds 650,000 seized ballots as the California Supreme Court weighs whether he must return them to state officials.
item.content:encoded:
Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco remains defiant as the California Supreme Court deliberates whether he has to return approximately 650,000 ballots he seized from a November 2025 special election on redistricting.

The court heard arguments Monday from Bianco’s lawyers and from California, where state Attorney General Rob Bonta launched a legal challenge to Bianco’s ballot seizures in March, ordering him to return the ballots.

Bianco, however, refused, arguing through his legal team that he had a legal obligation to investigate the ballots after receiving a complaint.

"I did this, and this was legal," Bianco told reporters. "I went a different route. They are legal. Both routes are legal. It's just their side doesn't like the route I chose."

DOJ DEMANDS 865K DETROIT BALLOTS, THREATENING POSSIBLE LEGAL ACTION

Bianco is still holding the ballots, his lawyer Bradley Hertz told reporters Monday, arguing that they are evidence.

CALIFORNIA ACCUSED OF BLOCKING FEDERAL VOTER ROLL AUDIT AS DOJ ESCALATES PROBE OF ELECTION FRAUD CLAIMS

"The sheriff is holding that evidence, safeguarding it as a custodian for the court," Hertz said.

The ballots are from a November 2025 special election in which state voters decided on Proposition 50, a legislative redistricting measure that passed by more than 3.4 million votes, according to the California Secretary of State.

CALIFORNIA ELECTION LIMBO FUELED BY 4 PRESSURE POINTS DRAGGING OUT VOTE COUNT, EXPERT SAYS

Bianco, however, appeared to question whether the official count was valid.

"How strange, that now we have evidence that the machines counted something different than the ballots that we have, and an Attorney General runs in to stop that investigation so that we’ll never know," Bianco said outside the courthouse.

CALIFORNIA DOGE LEADER SLAMS NEWSOM, BONTA OVER STATE’S MASSIVE FRAUD ISSUES: "EVERY DAY IS OPPOSITE DAY"

In filing his March legal challenge to Bianco’s ballot seizures, Bonta joined the UCLA Voting Rights Project, which launched a separate legal challenge to Bianco’s actions.

"This is a sheriff that – despite the clear language in the California constitution, and in California government code, providing me direct supervision, authority over him – failed to comply with it," Bonta told reporters outside the courthouse Monday.

"He can read, he knows what it says, it makes his violations even more egregious," Bonta also said.

Bianco, for his part, challenged Bonta’s interpretation of California code. "If you take it word for word, in that context, it means that he has direct authority that if I’m not doing my job he can order me to do it and if I don’t do it he can do it for me. But he cannot stop an investigation."

Fox News Digital contacted the UCLA Voting Rights Project, the Riverside County Sheriff's Office and the California Attorney General's Office for further comment.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Trump taunts Canada on renaming Lake Ontario the 'Lake America' amid rising border trade rift
item.description: Trump floats renaming Lake Ontario to "Lake America" and accuses Mark Carney of fabricating claims about French-language demands in trade talks.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump escalated his war of words with Canada on Tuesday morning, floating a U.S. push to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" and accusing Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney of lying about the Trump administration's position on French-language protections.

"The United States is giving serious consideration to changing the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in that we don’t expect to [sic] doing much business with Ontario any longer," Trump wrote Tuesday morning on Truth Social.

Trump followed with another broadside aimed directly at Carney, rejecting claims the U.S. had sought concessions affecting the French language during the countries' recently collapsed trade negotiations.

A POPULAR COCKTAIL HAS A TRUMP TRADE PROBLEM YOU PROBABLY DIDN’T KNOW ABOUT

"I would never interfere with Canadians speaking French!" Trump wrote. "In fact, I have never even thought of doing such a stupid thing."

"This lie was made up by a weak and ineffective Prime Minister in an attempt to gain political support, which he has totally lost, from the people of Quebec," Trump added. "I love French Canadians!"

The posts marked the latest escalation in an increasingly bitter dispute between Washington and Ottawa after trade negotiations broke down late last week, triggering a new round of tariffs and threats of retaliation between the longtime allies.

OPINION: TRUMP MUST CLOSE THE BACK DOOR CHINA USES TO EXPLOIT NORTH AMERICAN TRADE

"We were not prepared to compromise on the protection of the French language and our culture," Carney said Saturday while announcing the suspension of negotiations, adding that those issues were "never on the table" for Canada.

Carney doubled down Monday while in Quebec, arguing that French-language protections viewed by the U.S. as trade irritants were fundamental rights in Canada. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, however, disputed Carney's characterization, calling the French-language dispute a "funny, fake story" and saying the U.S. objection instead centered on requirements affecting American streaming companies.

Ontario is Canada's most populous province and a key hub in the tightly integrated U.S.-Canadian auto industry. Lake Ontario is shared by Ontario and New York, making Trump's proposed name change another provocative shot at America's northern neighbor as the economic standoff deepens.

TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED

The president has previously used geographic names to make a political point, ordering the change of Gulf of Mexico to be called Gulf of America.

Vice President JD Vance traveled to Maine on Monday and delivered a lengthy defense of the administration's hard-line approach toward Canada, accusing Ottawa of treating Chinese goods more favorably than products coming from its American neighbor.

"They treat Chinese goods more fairly than they do the goods that come from the people of Maine: It’s insanity," Vance said during a question-and-answer session Monday in Brewer. "And what we’ve said to Canada is stop it."

Vance said the two countries had appeared close to an agreement before negotiations fell apart, blaming Canadian officials for bringing what he described as unreasonable demands to the table at the last minute.

Trump separately announced Monday that 50% tariffs on Canadian automobiles, auto parts, trucks and steel would take effect Jan. 1, 2027, accusing Canada of years of unfair treatment of American producers.

"Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years," Trump wrote Monday.

Despite the sharpening rhetoric, Vance left open the possibility Monday that Washington and Ottawa could eventually return to the negotiating table.

"I think that we should have a deal," Vance said. "We expect fairness in our trade policy."

item.title: Callaway admits it approved controversial Good Good woman-shoving ad in late-night statement
item.description: Callaway CEO Chip Brewer admitted the company approved the Good Good golf ad showing Garrett Clark shoving a woman before it was posted online.
item.content:encoded:
Callaway Golf has issued a second statement regarding the controversial advertisement with Good Good, this time admitting that it greenlit the since-deleted video showing a man shoving a woman to the ground.

Good Good, the popular YouTube golf channel that boasts more than 2 million subscribers, teamed up with Callaway for a special edition driver. In the advertisement promoting the golf club, Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark shoved member Alexis Miestowski to the turf.

The beginning of the advertisement focuses on Miestowski reaching for the driver in a golf bag. Seeing this, Clark sprints at her, shoves her to the ground with his forearms, and stands over her before saying, "Do not touch my new driver."

FRUSTRATED BUBBA WATSON CONFRONTS UNRULY FAN AT LIV GOLF INDIANAPOLIS IN INTENSE SCENE

After deleting the video from its social channels, Good Good apologized in a statement, explaining that the ad "ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand." We look forward to working together to ensure a more inclusive space in golf."

As questions continued to be asked about how the advertisement made it past production and was ultimately published online, Callaway CEO Chip Brewer released a statement just after 1 a.m. ET on Tuesday morning, owning up to the fact that the company approved the video before posting.

"Last week, Good Good Golf and Callaway posted a video to promote a co-branded driver. While the video was produced by Good Good, it was approved by Callaway prior to posting. That approval should never have happened. Mistakes were made, and we are taking the matter very seriously," the statement began.

"As we deal with the consequences of our mistake and complete our investigations, I want to make it clear that we sincerely apologize for the video. The content was inappropriate and does not reflect our values. To be clear: We are unequivocally against discrimination, domestic violence, or threatening behavior of any kind.

"As soon as we recognized the seriousness of the issue, it was escalated appropriately, and the video was immediately removed. Preliminary statements were issued by both Good Good and Callaway, and now this statement has followed. We are also conducting both internal and external investigations and have already made changes to our approval processes aimed at ensuring this will never happen again.

"We believe we have been a positive force for diversity and inclusion in the game of golf. This video was completely inconsistent with that. I assure you that we will learn from this and do better."

OutKick has reached out to Good Good for further comment and will update this story if there is a response.

The PGA Tour commented on the advertisement amid the backlash that Good Good received online.

"The PGA Tour believes in golf’s ability to bring people together and create a welcoming environment for all," the statement said. "We do not condone violence in any form, and the since-deleted video does not reflect our values or commitment to inclusivity and respect."
